title_as_printed: The maximum solubility of methane and Setschenow constant in various electrolyte solutions with 1, 3 and 5 wt% concentration.
property_description: maximum (saturation) methane concentration in aqueous solution, mg CH4 per L of solution (ppm = mg/L per Fig. 2 caption), at 30 C, methane at ambient pressure bubbled through at 3 L/min
pressure_note: ambient pressure (value not stated); pure methane flowing; not a measured quantity

value2.what: Setschenow constant from log10(S0/S)=Ks*C (Eq. 1), numerically per unit mass fraction (printed values equal 100 x log10(S0/S)/(wt%)); header says Ks/wt% but a hand check gives 2.47 for NaCl 1 wt% (S0 21.7, S 20.5 ppm) against printed 2.51

composition.other_species: salt name is in label rows (composition.salt); salts outside six-ion set: Al2(SO4)3, AlCl3, MgBr2, NaBr, KBr (MgSO4 and K2SO4 are inside the six-ion set); wt% basis (wt/wt vs wt/vol) not stated in the paper

extra_unmapped: Setschenow constant (calculated by authors from S0 and S)
conversion_needs: mg/L of solution to mole fraction needs solution density and CH4 molar mass; wt% is stated but whether it is wt/wt or wt/vol is not stated
notes: Pure-water row printed with '-' in concentration and Ks; encoded as label row 'Water' (composition none) plus data row. P is only 'ambient'; 101.325 kPa assumed constant per SPEC 8 wording.
